02

SPOT SALES RED FLAGS

Turn warning signs
into your next good question.

Drawing on Salesforce’s approach to opportunity management, review an FP consultation through six adapted checks. Bring client concerns and missing information into view before moving to a proposal.

TRY A REQUEST LIKE THIS

“What are the red flags in this consultation? Show the evidence, what to ask next, and who should act by when.”

SIMYConsultation reviewIllustrative UI

SATO FAMILY / UNDERSTANDING NEEDS

Clarify first. Then prepare the proposal.

Red flags 2To confirm 3Confirmed 1

Red flag: a concern expressed by the client. To confirm: missing or outdated information. Neither means the opportunity is lost.

Budget & monthly commitment

Red flag

The client says a higher monthly commitment would be difficult.

Evidence and a question to ask
Example evidence
Meeting note 18:20: “It would be difficult to increase our monthly commitments.”
Next question
How much would you like to keep available each month for your daily life?

Decision-makers & family agreement

Red flag

The partner who shares the decision is not yet comfortable.

Evidence and a question to ask
Example evidence
Meeting note 22:10: “My wife and I decide together, but she isn’t comfortable yet.”
Next question
What is your partner most concerned about?

Timing & decision criteria

To confirm

The target date and comparison criteria have not been confirmed.

Evidence and a question to ask
Example evidence
Meeting record: no entry for the home purchase date or comparison criteria.
Next question
By when would you like to decide, and what would you need to know?

Engagement & stalled progress

To confirm

No further conversation is recorded after the last meeting.

Evidence and a question to ask
Example evidence
Activity history: no contact logged since the last meeting. Actual contact needs checking.
Next question
Has anything changed since we last spoke?

Next action, owner & due date

To confirm

“Follow up later” has no assigned owner or date.

Evidence and a question to ask
Example evidence
Next-action record: no owner or due date entered.
Next question
Who should we contact, when, and by which method?

Client needs

Confirmed

Wants to plan for housing and education together.

Evidence and a question to ask
Example evidence
Meeting note 12:40: “I want to plan for a home and education together.”
Next question
Which goal would you like to prepare for first?

PROPOSED NEXT ACTION / ADVISOR REVIEW NEEDED

Clarify monthly commitments and each partner’s priorities.

Owner: assigned FP. Proposed timing: by the day before the next meeting. Confirm the contact and timing with the client before scheduling.

Practice these questions on iOS ↓

Before progressing: the FP rechecks affordability, family agreement and comparison criteria, and consults a colleague or manager when needed.

Fictional client and illustrative screen. This example supports an advisor’s review; it does not automatically determine close probability or suitability.

Assessment approach and references

Needs, budget, decision-makers and timing adapt the BANT dimensions described by Salesforce. Engagement and next actions add a review of progress. The six checks and examples are tailored here to FP consultations.

  • Salesforce Trailhead — Opportunity management and warning signs
  • Salesforce Trailhead — Lead qualification, including BANT
  • Salesforce — Pipeline progress and next steps

QUESTIONS FROM A SIMILAR CASE

  1. Start with changes in daily life

    What changed most when your child was born?

  2. Make the goals concrete

    When would you like to buy a home?

  3. Understand who decides together

    What have you already agreed on as a couple?
